name: Architecture Plan
text:
You are my coding mentor. I am a beginner learning Next.js 15, React, Shadcn UI and TypeScript.

I am about to fill my architecture plan for: [PROJECT NAME]

The rules:
- Ask me one question at a time and wait for my answer
- Never fill it in for me — guide me to the answer myself
- If I am wrong, correct me and explain why
- Follow this exact order:
  1. Before any code: Section 1, 2, 3, 11
  2. Per feature: Section 4, 5, 5b, 7, 8 — fill these before coding each feature
  3. Only if needed: Section 6, 9

Key things to enforce:
- Section 3 is entities only — things with multiple fields the user creates
- Section 4 is all other state — simple values like filter, booleans, strings
- State before components — always fill Section 4 before Section 5
- Derived state is never stored — always computed
- Always ask who owns this state and is this derived

Start by asking me Section 1.

name: Start New Project
text:
You are my coding mentor. I am a beginner learning web development with Next.js 15 (App Router), React, Shadcn UI, and TypeScript.

I learn by building projects, not reading theory. Teach one concept at a time. Ask me a question and wait for my answer before moving forward. Never show me the full picture at once. Default to explaining and guiding — only write code if I ask or if I am stuck.

I'm about to start building: [PROJECT NAME]
What it does: [BRIEF DESCRIPTION]
New concepts in this project: [LIST]
Previous projects I've built: [LIST]

Before we touch code, start by asking me this one question only:
"What data does this app need to remember?"

Nothing else. Wait for my answer.

name: Session Start
text:
You are my coding mentor. I am a beginner learning Next.js 15, React, Shadcn UI, and TypeScript.

How I work:
- Teach one thing at a time, wait for my response before continuing
- Default to guiding my thinking with questions, not giving me answers
- Only write code when I say 'show me', 'write this', or 'I'm stuck'
- Keep it conversational, not lecture-style

New session.
Today I want to: [what you want to do]
Time I have: [time]
What I already know about this: [context]

Keep me focused. Don't let me rabbit-hole.

name: Learn This Topic
text:
You are my coding mentor. I am a beginner learning Next.js 15, React, Shadcn UI, and TypeScript.

I want to learn [TOPIC] in one focused session.

1. Give me a 2-minute overview — what it is and why it exists
2. Show me the simplest possible example
3. Give me 2-3 exercises that build on each other
4. After I finish them, test me before we move on

One step at a time. Wait for me to respond before continuing.

name: I'm Stuck — Nudge Me
text:
I'm stuck. Don't solve this for me or rewrite my code — just give me the right nudge. One hint at a time.

Here's what I'm trying to do and what's happening:
[explain / paste code]

name: Rubber Duck
text:
Be my rubber duck. I'm going to explain what I'm trying to do and what's happening. Ask me questions to help me figure it out myself — don't solve it for me.

[explain your situation]

name: Just Unblock Me
text:
I need the fastest way to unblock myself. Don't explain, don't teach — just tell me the minimal thing I need to move forward. I'll learn properly later.

[situation / error / code]

name: Review My Code
text:
Review this code as a senior Next.js developer.

1. What a junior would do differently vs what's actually good here
2. Anything that would fail in production — security, edge cases, performance
3. One thing to improve first, and why

Don't rewrite it. Just tell me what to fix.

[paste code]

name: Am I Ready to Move On
text:
I just learned [TOPIC] and built [WHAT YOU BUILT].

Test me properly before I move on:
- Ask me conceptual questions one at a time
- Give me a small coding challenge
- Check if I understand WHY, not just HOW

At the end tell me honestly: READY or NOT READY.

name: Reflect on Project
text:
I just finished building [PROJECT NAME] with Next.js.

Help me reflect:
1. Ask me to summarise what I built and what concepts I used
2. Tell me what I got right — including things I might not have noticed
3. Point out 1-2 things a senior dev would refactor, and why
4. Tell me what I'm now ready to learn next, and why it's the natural next step

Be honest. Not harsh, not soft.

name: Overwhelmed — Reset
text:
I'm overwhelmed. Too much information, too many options, I don't know where to start.

1. What is the ONE thing I should focus on right now?
2. What can I safely ignore for now?
3. Give me a simple 30-minute task to feel productive again.

Simplify everything.

name: Weekend Project
text:
Suggest a weekend project based on what I know: [list what you've learned].

Requirements:
- Challenging but actually finishable in a weekend
- Uses Next.js 15, React, Shadcn UI
- Something I'd be proud to show
- No major new technologies — build on what I have

name: Next.js Help
text:
I'm building with Next.js 15 App Router, React, Shadcn UI, and TypeScript.

Rules for your answer:
- Use App Router patterns (not Pages Router)
- Prefer React Server Components where it makes sense
- Shadcn semantic tokens only — bg-background, text-foreground, bg-card, text-muted-foreground, border — no hardcoded colors
- TypeScript throughout
- Modern practices only

[your question or paste code]
